title: Bundle of models R_F=W_F x_{O(nu)} P(nu) requires a structure-group action on the filling W_F (not constructed)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location.** `sec:global` (definition of the resolved tube) and `lem:tube`.

**The gap.** The global resolved tube over a stratum $C$ is defined as the associated fiber bundle
$$R_F := W_F\times_{O(\nu)} P(\nu)\ \to\ C,$$
justified by "$W_F$ depends only on the isomorphism class of $(F,V)$" and is "built canonically from the orthogonal slice." For this associated-bundle construction to be defined, the structure group $O(\nu)$ (or the relevant $F$-normalizer/holonomy reduction $O(m)\cap N_{O(m)}(\rho_F)$) must **act on the fiber $W_F$**, extending the linear action on $\partial W_F = S(V)=S^{m-1}$.

**Why this fails.** $W_F$ is produced by a **non-canonical** sequence of interior surgeries on an arbitrary null-bordism. There is **no** natural $O(m)$-action on $W_F$; and in general a **linear group action on a sphere does not extend over a chosen filling** (an extension would force the filling to be highly symmetric, e.g. a disk). So the fiber $W_F$ carries only the finite $F$-action, **not** the continuous structure-group action required to form $R_F=W_F\times_{O(\nu)}P(\nu)$.

Consequently:
1. The resolved tube $R_F$ is **not constructed** for $\dim C>0$; only its boundary sphere bundle $S(\nu)$ is canonical/natural.
2. `lem:tube` compares the two fibrations $R_F\to C$ and $N_F\to C$ over $C$ via "Leray–Hirsch/comparison of the two fibrations"; with $R_F$ undefined, this comparison has no basis.

**Fix options.** (a) Perform the surgeries **fiberwise/parametrized over $C$** (controlled or block surgery), constructing a genuine bundle of fillings with the bundle's structure group; prove the parametrized surgery obstructions vanish rationally. (b) Or construct a model $W_F$ that is genuinely **natural** in $(F,V)$ (functorial under the slice automorphism group), which is a strong requirement and must be proved. Either way the bare assertion "$R_F=W_F\times_{O(\nu)}P(\nu)$ is well defined" is unjustified.
